key.title: Make a key
key.intro: hubspot reads your deals, contacts and companies from one HubSpot account. It changes nothing there.
key.service:
A super admin, or a user with HubSpot's **Developer tools access** permission, does this once in HubSpot:

1. Open **Development**, then **Keys → Service keys** in the left menu. Some accounts show it under **Settings → Integrations → Service keys** instead.
2. Click **Create service key** and name it *WireCat*.
3. Click **Add new scope**, tick each read scope below, and click **Update**. A key gets only the scopes its maker has.
4. Click **Create** and confirm.

HubSpot's guide: https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/developer-platform/build-apps/authentication/account-service-keys

The read scopes:
key.leads: On Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise, add `crm.objects.leads.read` to read leads too. Add `tickets` if you want `api` to read tickets.
key.private.title: Already have a legacy private app?
key.private: HubSpot stopped new private apps on 26 October 2026, but an existing one's token still works. Give it the same read scopes, then copy its access token from the app's **Auth** tab.
token.title: Paste the key
token.where: In **Keys → Service keys**, click the key's name, then **Show** and **Copy**. A private app's token is on its **Auth** tab. Both start with `pat-`.
token.label: Service key or access token
token.hint: Kept in your system keyring or, without one, in a file only you can read.
token.rights: The key reads only what its scopes allow. Each profile signs in to its own HubSpot account: a second profile on the same account is refused.
check.title: Checking the key
check.body: hubspot asks HubSpot which account the key belongs to. It saves the key only if HubSpot answers.
failed.title: The check did not pass
failed.body: The key did not pass hubspot's check, so nothing was saved. Check the key and your connection, then try again.
